clue.text: Lack of confidence as result of scrutiny, i.e. being mistreated

indicators.note: words that are mistreated are knocked about, so their letters end up in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the abbreviation's two letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone loses their nerve because they are being picked over and badly treated under close examination.
explanation.definitionFit: Insecurity is the state of feeling unsure of oneself, a direct synonym for a lack of confidence.

clue.text: Uncertain short time after leader is removed

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, and here that letter is taken away

blocks.note: a jiffy is a moment

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure how long they have left once their boss has been ousted.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is an informal word for doubtful or of questionable reliability.

clue.text: Opposition elected replacement

blocks.note: to take a stand is to offer opposition
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: An opposition party has chosen someone new to take over.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in is a substitute who takes another person's place for a while.

clue.text: Lawyer with questions involving sex crime and arson

indicators.note: to involve is literally to roll up or entangle, so these words are tangled together into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A barrister puts questions in a trial about a sexual offence and a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is thin: 'involving' has to be read as tangling up the words that follow it, and 'and' just joins the two pieces of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-examiner is the advocate who questions the other side's witness in court.

clue.text: Snappy answer is concerning, and wrong

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
a tort is a civil wrong in law; 'and' adds it on

explanation.surface: A sharp reply is judged both relevant and mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: TORT is the legal term for a civil wrong, such as negligence.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a quick, sharp reply, often witty or angry.

clue.text: Protection for furniture cut from suitable material

indicators.note: a piece cut from something is part of it, so the letters lie inside the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a furniture cover from the right fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A table mat is placed under hot dishes to guard the surface of the table.

clue.text: What I'm referring to that is heartless?

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone points to something and asks whether it is unfeeling.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the pronoun a speaker uses for the thing near at hand that they mean.

clue.text: Husband wearing suit in warm indoor locations

indicators.note: whatever is wearing clothes sits inside them, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: one of the four suits in a pack of cards
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A man in a suit is sitting somewhere snug at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearths are fireplaces, the warm spots inside a house.

clue.text: Reduce or lessen dire changes

indicators.note: a change alters the form, so the preceding words are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to cut back or soften awful changes.
explanation.definitionFit: To slenderise is to slim down, which is to reduce one's size or weight.

clue.text: Nuisance for driver revealed at top speed

blocks.note: a flat tyre, a motorist's headache
a secret that is revealed is out

explanation.surface: A motorist's problem comes to light while racing along.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat out is an idiom for going as fast as possible.

clue.text: Spy many years in captivity

blocks.note: James Bond, the fictional spy
an age is a very long period

explanation.surface: A secret agent spends a long time locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Bondage is slavery or servitude, a state of being held captive.

clue.text: Supporting one's people, revise an initial cost

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to rework a starting price while backing your own side.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationalistic describes fervent loyalty to one's own nation, so it means backing one's people.

clue.text: Lacking sense of direction as a setter, I did no wrong?

indicators.note: something done wrong comes out jumbled, so the preceding words are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A confused crossword setter wonders aloud whether they made any mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: the setter claims to have done no wrong while the letters are being done wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorientated is the British form of disoriented: confused about where one is or which way to go.

clue.text: North of port, two letters he has delivered

indicators.note: in a down entry, north of means placed above, so the second piece comes first

blocks.note: the two letters the word he has are H and E, written out as H AND E
the Channel port in Kent

explanation.surface: Something about a pair of letters handed in at a northern harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'two letters he has' literally: the word 'he' has two letters, H and E, giving H-AND-E. Dover is England's main ferry port facing France.
explanation.definitionFit: Handed over means passed to someone else, the same as delivered.

clue.text: Fire about ten main people finally, in addition

definitions.note: an annexe is an added building, a noun like addition

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of each of the words just before it
about means around, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: to axe someone is to fire them
the last letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A sacking hits about ten key staff at the end, on top of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extension or addition built onto a main building.

clue.text: Motorist accommodating old reveller

indicators.note: something accommodating gives room to a guest, holding it inside

blocks.note: someone who uses a car
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A driver gives a lift to an elderly partygoer.
explanation.definitionFit: A carouser drinks and makes merry noisily, so is a reveller.

clue.text: Rushing south where invader was engaged in battle

definitions.text: where invader was engaged in battle

blocks.note: hasting is an old word for hurrying
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Hurrying south to the place where a foreign army fought.
explanation.walkthrough: William of Normandy's invasion in 1066 was decided at the Battle of Hastings; it was actually fought at the nearby town now called Battle, hence the pun in 'engaged in battle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastings is the Sussex coastal town that gave its name to the 1066 conquest battle.

clue.text: I had reversed pieces of proof, creating problems

indicators.note: reversed means turned back to front, so the contraction is read from its end

blocks.note: the contraction I'd
a lemma is a subsidiary proposition proved on the way to a theorem

explanation.surface: A mathematician turned around parts of an argument and ended up with difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult choice between options, so dilemmas are awkward problems.

clue.text: Small child in cap subject to restriction

blocks.note: a lid caps a container
a mite is a tiny child

explanation.definitionFit: Limited means restricted or kept within set bounds.

clue.text: Part of Balkans, a Slavic state

blocks.note: the run of letters across these words

explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'state' look like a European nation; it is one of the US states.
explanation.definitionFit: Kansas is a state in the central United States.

clue.text: First in school, except when not bright, naturally

indicators.note: first in points to the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: its opening letter
unless means except if

explanation.surface: Coming top of the class, except when a pupil is not naturally clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not bright' suggests dim-witted, but 'naturally' steers it to light from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunless means without sunshine, so dull in natural light.

clue.text: Head who might be caught unawares?

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for the head
second meaning: someone dozing, easily surprised

explanation.surface: A school head who could be surprised.
explanation.walkthrough: Napper is old British slang for the head; read the other way, it is one who naps, and a sleeper is easy to catch off guard.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for the skull and also names a person taking a short sleep.

clue.text: Fiend runs into position for protest

a station is a post or position

explanation.definitionFit: A demonstration is a public march or rally held as a protest.

clue.text: Work in college, mainly, or kind of farm

clue.text: Experienced kind of doctor managed without drug

to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: An animal doctor coped without medication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it carries its old meaning of outside.

clue.text: Person with complaint that's slow to complain

blocks.note: first meaning: someone under medical care, a complaint being an illness

explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a sick person under treatment; the adjective means able to wait calmly without fuss.

clue.text: Decorate anew using colour circle

blocks.note: red is a colour
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: Repainting a room with a colour wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: To redo a room is to refurbish or redecorate it.

clue.text: Cost raised after Charlie's replaced, banished from company

indicators.note: Charlie is the radio code word for the letter C, and replaced means put back in a different place

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A price went up once someone named Charlie was replaced, and he was then expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one letter moves: take the C from the front of 'Cost raised' and re-place it after OSTRA. Charlie is C in the radio alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: To ostracise is to exclude someone from society or a group.
